title: New Curriculum, New Chance – Retrieval Augmented Generation for Lesson Planning in Ugandan Secondary Schools. Prototype Quality Evaluation.
venue: Ndejje University Second Annual Research Dissemination Symposium 2024
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of low-quality or absent lesson planning in Ugandan secondary schools, especially in the context of a new competency-based curriculum that has made existing lesson plans obsolete. The authors ask whether a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system can generate lesson plans that meet necessary technical standards for classroom use.

The intervention is a prototype lesson-plan generator built with Cohere LLM, sentence embeddings, and LangChain. It retrieves information from government-accredited secondary school textbooks and generates lesson plans in the Ugandan lesson-plan format. The prototype was made available on a public website and tested on three Secondary 1 textbooks: ICT, Mathematics, and History (including Political Education).

The study context is Ugandan secondary schools, with the intended users being teachers. The prototype produced 24 lesson plans, which were evaluated by three independent raters using an adapted Lesson Plan Analysis Protocol (LPAP). The authors report average scores of about 75-80%, with none below 65%, suggesting that the generated plans were technically strong and comparable to or better than human-created lesson plans in prior East African studies.

The paper also identifies important risks and limitations, especially hallucination: one generated plan addressed the wrong topic when the source textbook had insufficient material. The authors note that the system may still require teacher judgment and future safeguards such as confidence indicators or plausibility checks. Overall, they conclude that RAG has promise for supporting lesson planning in Ugandan classrooms, while cautioning that content accuracy and ethical considerations still need further work.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generative AI lesson-plan system built with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), using a large language model, sentence embeddings, and LangChain to generate customized lesson plans from government-approved textbooks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper developed and evaluated the NDU Lesson Plan Generator (NLPG) prototype for generating lesson plans for Ugandan secondary school teachers aligned to the new curriculum.

findings.finding_summary: Across 24 generated lesson plans, three independent raters using the Lesson Plan Analysis Protocol (LPAP) reported average quality scores of 75-80%, which the authors describe as 'very good lesson plan' quality. None of the plans scored below 65%, although one plan (History07.pdf) addressed the wrong topic due to insufficient source content.
findings.measure: LPAP-based technical quality of generated lesson plans

quality_tier_rationale: This is a prototype evaluation working paper with a quasi-random generation protocol and expert ratings, but it is not a controlled trial and evaluates only technical quality. The evidence is informative but limited and therefore fits a yellow tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported lesson-plan quality is high, but no standardized effect size is reported and the study does not test classroom learning outcomes. Impact is therefore promising but unclear at the level required for higher tiers.
